documents.title: Sickle Cell Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Spring check. Made it through the winter without a crisis. Hip unchanged. Hematology last seen in February, same plan per pt. Still has not booked the eye exam, gave him the number again.
Meds: hydroxyurea 1000 mg daily, folic acid 1 mg daily, penicillin VK 250 BID.
Exam: comfortable. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, spleen tip palpable, nontender.
A/P: HbSS stable. CBC today since hematology's results don't always reach us. Physical in September.

documents.title: CBC
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hemoglobin is right around 9, same as the last couple of years. White count and platelets at your usual. All good.

conditions.label: Splenic laceration
conditions.note: atraumatic, subcapsular hematoma, setting of infectious mononucleosis; managed nonoperatively

reports.text: Limited abdominal ultrasound, ED. The spleen is enlarged. A hypoechoic area along the splenic margin is suggestive of a subcapsular hematoma. Liver of normal echotexture. Gallbladder without stones. Kidneys without hydronephrosis.
reports.conclusion: Enlarged spleen with a hypoechoic area suggestive of subcapsular hematoma.

documents.title: Emergency Department Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, 06/13/2025, evening.
25 y/o M, HbSS, functional asplenia. Abrupt severe LUQ pain this evening going up into the L shoulder. For about a week before: sore throat, fevers, worn out, better with rest and fluids over the last couple of days. No fall, no blow to the abdomen, no sports.
Meds: hydroxyurea 1000 mg daily, folic acid 1 mg daily, PCN VK 250 mg BID. NKDA.
BP 90/60, HR 120, RR 22, T 37.8.
Pale, sweaty. Abd: LUQ tender with guarding; bowel sounds present and normal; no rebound, not rigid.
Hgb 9.8, WBC 15,000, plt 250,000. AST 45, ALT 50. Monospot positive.
Bedside/formal US: enlarged spleen, hypoechoic area c/w subcapsular hematoma.
Imp: atraumatic splenic laceration with subcapsular hematoma in the setting of recent infectious mononucleosis. Fluid resuscitation started, surgery consulted, admitted.

documents.title: Discharge Summary
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
Admit 06/13/2025 - Discharge 06/17/2025. Surgical service.
Dx: splenic laceration, subcapsular hematoma, nonoperative management. Recent mononucleosis.
Course: IV fluids, bed rest, serial hemoglobins, which held steady. Heart rate and blood pressure normalized within the first day. No transfusion. No operation. Hydroxyurea and home meds continued. Pain controlled and tolerating diet at discharge.
Instructions: no lifting over 10 lb, no contact sports or strenuous activity until seen in surgery clinic. Return for worse abdominal pain, dizziness or fainting.
Follow-up: PCP 1 week; surgery clinic 6-8 weeks.

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit. Records from the regional hospital reviewed (ED note and discharge summary arrived 6/19; spoke with pt by phone 6/18 to set this up).
Admitted 6/13-6/17 with an atraumatic splenic laceration and subcapsular hematoma after a week of what turned out to be mono (monospot +). Managed without surgery, no transfusion.
Today: LUQ soreness down to a 2, only with twisting. Sore throat gone, no fever since discharge. Eating fine. Staying off work this week, library is holding his hours.
Meds unchanged, reconciled: hydroxyurea 1000 mg daily, folic acid 1 mg daily, penicillin VK 250 mg BID.
Exam: tired-looking but comfortable. Abdomen soft, mild LUQ tenderness, no guarding; spleen not examined deeply.
A/P
1. Splenic laceration, healing, nonoperative. Repeat CBC today. Keep surgery's restrictions: no lifting over 10 lb, no contact or strenuous activity until surgery clinic (booked for August). Any sudden pain, dizziness or faint = ED.
2. HbSS / asplenia: no changes. Fever rule as always.
Work note given for this week.

documents.title: Cleared
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Saw the surgeon today. He said my spleen is healed enough and I can go back to normal stuff. They didn't give me papers. Just letting you know.

documents.title: RE: Cleared
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Great news, thanks for telling us. We'll ask the surgery clinic for their note. See you for your physical in September.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual.
Interval: June admission for atraumatic splenic laceration with mono, nonoperative. Surgery clinic cleared him in mid-August per his report (their note never came; re-requested). No abdominal pain now. Back at full hours at work and doing fall classes.
No crises this year.
Meds: hydroxyurea 1000 mg daily, folic acid 1 mg daily, penicillin VK 250 mg BID. NKDA.
Never smoker, alcohol rare.
ROS negative.
Exam: well. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, nontender, spleen tip palpable as on prior exams. R hip end-range IR pain as before.
PHQ-2 1.
A/P
- Splenic laceration: resolved, cleared by surgery. Off the active list.
- HbSS: stable. Annual labs including liver tests (AST/ALT were up a little with the mono).
- Splenomegaly: unchanged.
- Vaccines: flu and COVID in October. MenACWY booster due next June.
- Eye exam overdue; referral placed so the eye office calls him.

documents.title: Labs from your physical

documents.body: Your liver tests are back to normal after the mono, hemoglobin is near your usual 9, kidneys and urine fine.

documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu R deltoid, COVID L deltoid, both 2025-26 formulas. No complaints. Tolerated, observed, discharged.

events.reason: Jaundice and dark urine after transfusion

conditions.label: Sickle cell disease with vaso-occlusive crisis
conditions.note: admitted 11/29-12/3 at the regional hospital with red cell transfusion 12/2, per patient and ED note; no records received

documents.title: Emergency Department Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, 12/12/2025.
25 y/o M with HbSS and functional asplenia; splenic laceration about six months ago, managed without surgery. Two days of increasing fatigue, yellow eyes and dark urine. Was admitted here 11/29-12/3 for a pain crisis and got a red cell transfusion on 12/2, ten days ago.
Meds: folic acid 1 mg daily, penicillin VK 250 mg BID, hydroxyurea 1000 mg daily. NKDA.
T 37.8, BP 130/80, HR 105, RR 18.
Scleral icterus. Mild splenomegaly. No rash. No lymphadenopathy.
Hgb 7.0 (baseline about 9). T bili 3.5, direct 0.8. LDH 600. Haptoglobin <10. Retic 15%. DAT positive; negative before the transfusion.
Imp: delayed hemolytic transfusion reaction. Blood bank notified, hematology consulted. Admitted for monitoring; avoid further transfusion if at all possible.

documents.title: Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Admit 12/12/2025 - Discharge 12/14/2025.
Dx: delayed hemolytic transfusion reaction after 12/2 transfusion. HbSS.
Course: observed with daily labs; hemoglobin held without further transfusion. Blood bank antibody workup sent, results to his hematologist. Hematology saw him in house. Folic acid and hydroxyurea continued. No pain crisis during the stay.
Important: any future transfusion only after his hematologist and the blood bank are contacted.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; hematology clinic early January.

conditions.label: Sickle cell disease with vaso-occlusive crisis

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM. ED note and discharge summary received yesterday and reviewed. We had no records from the 11/29-12/3 crisis admission; pt filled in the history: pain crisis in the cold, admitted, one unit of blood on 12/2. Then on 12/10 he started getting tired and yellow, and urine went dark, back to the ED 12/12. Delayed hemolytic transfusion reaction, DAT positive, no more blood given, home 12/14.
Today: still tired but better each day. Eyes less yellow, urine lighter. Pain from the crisis gone. No fever, chest pain, SOB.
Meds reconciled, unchanged: hydroxyurea 1000 mg daily, folic acid 1 mg daily, penicillin VK 250 mg BID.
Exam: tired but comfortable. Mild scleral icterus. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, spleen tip palpable, nontender.
A/P
1. DHTR, improving clinically. CBC and bili today. Recheck in 3-4 weeks. Added a transfusion alert to his chart: contact hematology and blood bank before any transfusion.
2. VOC late Nov, resolved.
3. HbSS: hematology early January.
ED for fever, worsening jaundice, chest pain or breathlessness.

documents.title: Yesterday's labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hemoglobin is a bit higher than at the ED and bilirubin is coming down. That fits with the reaction settling. Recheck around January 12. Rest up over the holidays.

conditions.label: Delayed hemolytic transfusion reaction
conditions.note: transfusion caution remains: contact hematology and blood bank before any transfusion

documents.title: Recheck labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Darnell, hemoglobin is back to 8.9, retic 8%, bilirubin 2.6. That's basically your baseline, so the transfusion reaction has run its course. The transfusion warning stays on your chart for good. Did you get in to hematology?

documents.title: RE: Recheck labs
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Yes last Thursday. They said same meds and they have the antibody stuff on file. I feel normal again.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine. Feels well, energy back. No crises since November. Hematology in January: no changes, antibody results on file with them.
Eye office never reached him after the September referral; he called them himself last week and is waiting for a date.
Meds: hydroxyurea 1000 mg daily, folic acid 1 mg daily, penicillin VK 250 mg BID.
Exam: well. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, spleen tip palpable, nontender.
A/P: HbSS stable. Transfusion alert stays. Physical in June with yearly labs and MenACWY booster.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly exam, 26 y/o with HbSS.
Since last physical: VOC admission with transfusion late Nov, then delayed hemolytic transfusion reaction in Dec, recovered by January. Nothing since. Splenic laceration last June, healed.
Eye appointment is set for July.
Meds: hydroxyurea 1000 mg daily, folic acid 1 mg daily, penicillin VK 250 mg BID. NKDA. Transfusion alert on chart.
SH: library part time, classes. Never smoker; alcohol rare.
ROS negative.
Exam: well. HEENT normal. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, spleen tip palpable, nontender. R hip end-range IR pain, same as always. No leg ulcers.
PHQ-2 0.
A/P: HbSS stable. Annual CBC, CMP, urine albumin. MenACWY booster today (5 yr). Flu/COVID this fall; sickle cell visit in September.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: All stable. Hemoglobin about 9, kidneys normal, urine protein negative. No changes.

documents.title: Pharmacy Refill Request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Folic acid 1 mg refill request from pharmacy, approved per protocol, 90 days x3. Hydroxyurea on the same fax redirected to hematology.
